candidates.exact_span: Regulations contained in 40 CFR §122.44 requires that NPDES permit limits are developed that meet the more stringent of either technology-based effluent limitation guidelines, numerical and/or narrative water quality standard-based effluent limits, or the previous permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The more-stringent-of selection rule governs which numeric or narrative limit is enforceable when multiple limit types could apply; a different reading of how this rule interacts with Outfall 001 limits could change the applicable discharge limit used for compliance comparison.

candidates.exact_span: Regulations found in 40 CFR 411.13 and 411.17 define BAT and BCT effluent limitations, respectively, for cement manufacturing non-leaching process, and 40 CFR 411.37 defines BCT effluent guidelines for materials storage piles runoff from cement manufacturing facilities.
candidates.computation_change_reason: These citations identify which ELG subparts could supply enforceable numeric limits; interpreting whether Outfall 001 discharges fall under non-leaching process versus materials storage piles runoff could change which ELG-based limits are considered applicable.

candidates.exact_span: Effluent limitations established at Outfall 001 in the current permit regulate overflows from Quarry #1 pond which stores storm runoff and process water effluent from plant areas.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This passage defines the discharge scope and outfall association for enforceable limits and monitoring; a different interpretation of what Outfall 001 covers could change which reported measurements and requirements are tied to that outfall.

candidates.exact_span: The 40 CFR 411.37 ELG of 50 mg/l was the basis for establishment of TSS effluent limitation at Outfall 001.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This links the Outfall 001 TSS limit to a specific numeric ELG value; interpreting whether 50 mg/l is the operative enforceable limit versus explanatory background could change the numeric threshold used in exceedance evaluation.

candidates.exact_span: EPA did not establish 40 CFR 411.13 temperature limitation at Outfall 001 because discharges at Outfall 001 would be intermittent and the permit restricted discharges due to catastrophic or chronic precipitation events.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This states that a temperature numeric limit was not established and ties discharge occurrence to intermittent/restricted conditions; different readings could change whether temperature has an enforceable numeric limit, when monitoring is required, and how no-discharge or conditional periods should be classified for missing-result cases.

candidates.exact_span: The 40 CFR 411.17 TSS mass load limitation might not be applicable at Outfall 001 because the combination of storm runoff and process water.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The passage explicitly leaves mass-load limit applicability uncertain; treating this as applicable versus inapplicable would change whether a separate mass-based TSS limit enters the enforceable-limit computation.

candidates.exact_span: TSS reported maximum daily discharge did exceed the daily max limit of 50 mg/l.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This describes a prior daily-maximum exceedance against the 50 mg/l limit; interpreting its bearing on whether daily-maximum comparison remains operative versus superseded by proposed changes could affect which limit basis and comparison period are used.

candidates.exact_span: As a result, it is proposed in the draft permit that the permittee report 30-day average for TSS.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The proposed shift from daily-maximum framing to 30-day average reporting could change both the enforceable numeric comparison basis for TSS and the applicable monitoring/reporting obligation at Outfall 001.

candidates.exact_span: Water quality-based requirements are necessary where effluent limits more stringent than technology-based limits are necessary to maintain or achieve federal or state water quality limits.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This states when water quality-based limits supplement technology-based limits; interpreting whether such more-stringent WQBELs exist for Outfall 001 parameters could change which numeric limits are selected for compliance comparison.
